morningSummary: RadiantWaves Media's Midday Global Update examines a fast-moving international agenda. US envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff have arrived in Moscow for talks with Vladimir Putin following US-mediated negotiations in Abu Dhabi. Those talks produced an agreement to arrange a major prisoner exchange, but no breakthrough on territory or a ceasefire. In Gaza, an Israeli strike hit Nasser Hospital in Khan Younis. Gaza civil defence reported at least six deaths and 20 wounded; Israel's military said it targeted Hamas operatives, a claim that requires independent scrutiny. Indonesia's Vice-President Gibran Rakabuming Raka has submitted his resignation, with President Prabowo accepting it and parliament expected to follow constitutional procedures. France's 2027 presidential debate has taken an unexpected turn following judoka Teddy Riner's candidacy and President Emmanuel Macron's public encouragement. Moody's has reduced its 2026 French growth forecast to 0.2%. In Nigeria, the ADC leadership dispute and the implications for Atiku Abubakar's political plans remain subject to court proceedings and INEC's examination of the certified judgment. The DRC continues to face a severe Ebola outbreak, while Kenya has discharged its last known patient and entered a 42-day monitoring period. G7 foreign ministers have warned that China's activities east of Taiwan threaten regional stability and freedom of navigation. More than 40 European leaders and guests are meeting in Dublin to discuss Ukraine and European security. This edition distinguishes confirmed developments from allegations, official claims and unresolved questions.

featured.title: US Envoys in Moscow as Ukraine Peace Effort Enters Critical Phase
featured.summary: Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff have arrived in Moscow to brief Vladimir Putin on US-mediated discussions in Abu Dhabi. A proposed prisoner exchange offers a humanitarian step, but major disagreements remain.
featured.content:
US envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff arrived in Moscow on Thursday for talks with Russian President Vladimir Putin. Their visit follows two days of US-mediated negotiations involving Russian and Ukrainian representatives in Abu Dhabi.

The Abu Dhabi discussions produced an agreement to arrange another major prisoner exchange. However, the negotiations did not resolve the central disagreements over territory, sovereignty and post-war security arrangements. Ukraine has rejected Russia's demand that it surrender the whole of the Donbas region as part of a settlement.

The US delegation is expected to brief Putin on the discussions and explore whether further negotiations can be organised. The envoys are also expected to meet Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy in Dublin after the Moscow visit. More than 40 European leaders and guests are meeting in the Irish capital to discuss Ukraine and wider European security.

The role of European governments remains an important issue. European leaders have argued that decisions affecting the continent's security cannot be made without meaningful European participation. Russia has expressed reservations about European involvement in the negotiations.

WHY IT MATTERS: A prisoner exchange can bring relief to families, but it is not a ceasefire or a peace agreement. The key tests will be whether the parties can make progress on territory, security guarantees and the participation of Ukraine and European partners.

WHAT HAPPENS NEXT: Attention will focus on the outcome of the Moscow meeting, the planned discussions with Zelenskyy, the possibility of wider European participation and whether the prisoner exchange can be implemented.

articles.excerpt: Kushner and Witkoff have arrived for talks with Putin after Abu Dhabi negotiations produced a proposed prisoner exchange but no breakthrough on territory or a ceasefire.

articles.title: Israeli Strike Hits Nasser Hospital in Southern Gaza, Six Reported Dead
articles.excerpt: Gaza civil defence reports at least six people killed and 20 wounded after a strike hit the hospital's surgery department. Israel says it targeted Hamas operatives.
articles.content:
An Israeli airstrike hit the surgery department of Nasser Hospital in Khan Younis, southern Gaza, early on Thursday. Gaza civil defence spokesperson Mahmoud Basal reported that at least six people were killed and 20 wounded. The dead included surgeon Rezik Abushira, according to medical officials.

Reuters footage showed extensive damage inside the hospital, with rubble and damaged equipment in corridors and rooms. Patients were evacuated as medical and emergency teams responded.

Israel's military said it targeted Hamas operatives allegedly operating inside the hospital. The allegation has not been independently verified. Hamas condemned the strike. The circumstances surrounding the alleged military activity and the precise events leading to the attack require independent investigation.

Hospitals and medical personnel receive special protection under international humanitarian law. That protection is central to the assessment of attacks on medical facilities, and all parties remain obliged to protect patients and civilians.

WHY IT MATTERS: Nasser Hospital is an important medical facility in southern Gaza. Damage to hospitals further reduces access to treatment for people already affected by conflict, displacement and shortages.

WHAT HAPPENS NEXT: Independent scrutiny of the circumstances, a fuller assessment of casualties and continued monitoring of the hospital's ability to provide care will be important.

articles.title: Indonesia Vice-President Gibran Resigns Amid Eligibility Controversy
articles.excerpt: Gibran Rakabuming Raka has submitted his resignation to parliament's upper house. President Prabowo Subianto has accepted it.
articles.content:
Indonesia's Vice-President Gibran Rakabuming Raka has submitted his resignation to parliament's upper house, according to Reuters. President Prabowo Subianto accepted the resignation and praised Gibran's work.

The resignation follows months of political controversy over Gibran's eligibility and educational credentials. Lawmakers had called for parliamentary action after court rulings concerning the qualifications used in his election process.

Under Indonesia's constitutional arrangements, parliament must declare the office vacant and the president is expected to nominate candidates for lawmakers to consider. The selection process is expected to be completed within 60 days.

The political consequences extend beyond the immediate vacancy. Gibran is the son of former President Joko Widodo, whose political influence remains an important factor in Indonesian politics. The resignation comes at a time of wider economic and political pressure on the administration.

WHY IT MATTERS: A vice-presidential resignation tests constitutional procedures and public confidence in political institutions. The replacement process will be closely watched by parliament, political parties and investors.

WHAT HAPPENS NEXT: Parliament's formal response, the president's nominations and the timetable for selecting a replacement will determine the next stage.

articles.title: Macron's Response to Teddy Riner Adds New Dimension to France's 2027 Race
articles.excerpt: The Olympic judo champion has announced his presidential candidacy. Macron publicly welcomed his decision to enter the political debate.
articles.content:
France's 2027 presidential debate has taken an unexpected turn following the announcement by Olympic judo champion Teddy Riner that he intends to run for president. President Emmanuel Macron publicly welcomed Riner's decision to enter the debate and drew comparisons with his own outsider campaign in 2017.

Riner has presented himself as a figure outside traditional party politics. He has spoken about national unity, France's public finances and the country's social challenges. However, a public announcement is only the beginning of a presidential campaign. A credible candidacy requires a detailed programme, a political organisation, alliances and the ability to meet the legal requirements for standing.

Macron cannot seek a third consecutive presidential term. His public comments have therefore attracted attention because they may influence the debate over who succeeds him. Le Monde reports that Macron was aware of Riner's plans before the announcement, but this does not establish that he organised the campaign.

WHY IT MATTERS: The development introduces another personality into an already competitive political landscape. It also raises questions about the influence of public figures outside established political parties.

WHAT HAPPENS NEXT: Riner's policy proposals, campaign organisation, political alliances and public support will determine whether the announcement becomes a substantial electoral challenge.

articles.title: ADC Legal Dispute: Atiku's Political Future Remains Subject to Court Process
articles.excerpt: The 5 November Federal High Court judgment affected the David Mark-led ADC leadership and Atiku Abubakar's nomination. The party says it is pursuing an appeal.
articles.content:
The African Democratic Congress remains involved in a legal dispute over its leadership and the processes that produced the leadership headed by David Mark. The Federal High Court judgment delivered on 5 November has implications for decisions taken under that leadership, including the process connected to Atiku Abubakar's nomination.

The ADC has rejected the ruling and says it is pursuing legal remedies. The Independent National Electoral Commission has indicated that it needs to examine the certified true copy of the judgment before determining its institutional response. The commission's position should be understood in the context of the actual court record and any subsequent orders.

It is important to distinguish between filing an appeal, applying for a stay of execution and obtaining an order that suspends the effect of a judgment. An appeal does not automatically overturn a ruling. The legal position can change if an appellate court issues further directions or orders.

WHY IT MATTERS: The dispute affects party administration, opposition organisation and the political plans of figures seeking to contest the 2027 election. A stable and lawful party structure is important for credible political competition.

WHAT HAPPENS NEXT: The certified judgment, appeal proceedings, any application for a stay and INEC's formal response are the developments to monitor. RadiantWaves Media will distinguish court findings from party statements and political interpretations.
articles.source: Premium Times; INEC statements; Nigerian media reports

articles.title: Moody's Cuts France's 2026 Growth Forecast to 0.2%
articles.excerpt: Moody's has reduced its French growth forecast, citing political uncertainty, higher bond yields and fiscal challenges.
articles.content:
Credit rating agency Moody's has reduced its forecast for French economic growth in 2026 to 0.2%, according to a report published on 11 November. The new projection is below the French government's target of 0.5% and the Bank of France's forecast of around 0.3%.

Moody's cited political uncertainty, higher bond yields and fiscal challenges as factors constraining growth. France is also facing difficult budget negotiations and pressure to manage its public debt, which is around 120% of gross domestic product.

The forecast is not a declaration that France is in recession. It is an assessment that economic growth is likely to be weak. Slower growth can reduce tax revenues, complicate deficit-reduction plans and affect investment and household confidence.

WHY IT MATTERS: France is one of the eurozone's largest economies. Weak growth and unresolved budget questions can affect public services, business confidence, borrowing costs and the wider European economy.

WHAT HAPPENS NEXT: Economic indicators, parliamentary budget negotiations, government decisions and further assessments by rating agencies will shape the outlook.

articles.title: France Signals Further EU Sanctions Against Russia
articles.excerpt: French officials say the European Union is expected to approve additional sanctions targeting entities and banks.
articles.content:
France says European Union governments are expected to approve another package of sanctions against Russia. French European Affairs Minister Benjamin Haddad said the proposed measures would target 150 additional entities and 50 banks, with France having proposed most of the entities.

The announcement comes as European leaders meet in Dublin to discuss Ukraine and wider security. The sanctions effort is part of continuing European pressure on Moscow following Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine.

Sanctions can restrict access to financial services, trade and other resources. Their practical effect depends on enforcement, coordination between governments and measures to prevent evasion. The announcement of a proposed package should not be confused with the formal adoption or implementation of the measures.

WHY IT MATTERS: The sanctions debate reflects Europe's attempt to maintain pressure on Russia while supporting Ukraine and managing the economic consequences of the war.

WHAT HAPPENS NEXT: The formal EU decision, the final list of targets and the implementation timetable will determine the scope of the measures.

articles.title: G7 Warns China's Activity East of Taiwan Threatens Regional Stability
articles.excerpt: G7 foreign ministers have warned that China's activities east of Taiwan threaten regional stability, freedom of navigation and international shipping.
articles.content:
G7 foreign ministers have warned that China's increasingly assertive activities in the waters east of Taiwan threaten regional stability, freedom of navigation and the safety of international shipping. The warning was included in a joint declaration following a meeting in Paris on 9 and 10 November.

The ministers reaffirmed their opposition to unilateral attempts to change the status quo through force or coercion and encouraged the peaceful resolution of cross-strait issues through constructive dialogue. Taiwan welcomed the statement and said it would continue strengthening its self-defence capabilities and resilience.

China regards Taiwan as part of its territory and rejects foreign criticism of its position. Taiwan's government rejects Beijing's sovereignty claim and maintains its own democratic political system.

WHY IT MATTERS: The Taiwan Strait is strategically important for international shipping, regional security and the global technology supply chain, including advanced semiconductor production.

WHAT HAPPENS NEXT: Diplomatic responses, military activity and efforts to maintain communication will be important indicators of whether tensions rise or restraint prevails.
articles.source: Reuters; G7 joint declaration; Taiwan Presidential Office

articles.title: DR Congo Ebola Outbreak Remains a Major Regional Health Emergency
articles.excerpt: The DRC has reported 11,042 confirmed cases and 5,387 related deaths in the latest available figures. Kenya has discharged its last known patient.
articles.content:
The Democratic Republic of Congo continues to face a serious Ebola outbreak caused by the Bundibugyo virus. The European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control reported 11,042 confirmed cases and 5,387 related deaths using figures available up to 9 November. Community transmission remains ongoing in the DRC.

The regional situation requires careful reporting. Kenya has discharged its last known patient and has begun a 42-day monitoring period. Kenya's outbreak involved nine confirmed cases, including two deaths. The final patient was discharged on 11 November, and the country could be declared free of the outbreak if no new cases are identified during the monitoring period.

Nigeria reported one case on 20 October involving a traveller with a history of travel to Uganda. The individual was medically evacuated to Switzerland, and 62 contacts were identified. This should not be presented as evidence of a sustained nationwide outbreak in Nigeria.

WHY IT MATTERS: Ebola response depends on early detection, contact tracing, safe treatment, infection prevention and public trust. Conflict and limited access to communities can make the response more difficult.

WHAT HAPPENS NEXT: Health authorities must continue surveillance, contact monitoring and cross-border coordination. Kenya's monitoring period must be completed without a new case before the outbreak can be declared over.
articles.source: European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control; WHO Africa

articles.title: Deadly Building Collapse in Brooklyn Triggers Investigation
articles.excerpt: At least two people have died and more than ten have been injured after a building collapsed in Brooklyn. The cause remains under investigation.
articles.content:
A three-storey residential building in Brooklyn, New York, collapsed on Wednesday, killing at least two people and injuring more than ten, according to reports from Reuters and New York officials.

Emergency crews responded to the scene and searched the debris. The building was next to a construction site where excavation work was taking place. However, the proximity of the construction work does not establish the cause of the collapse.

Authorities are investigating the building's condition, the work taking place nearby and whether relevant safety requirements were followed. Emergency officials have been working to establish the full number of people affected.

WHY IT MATTERS: The incident raises questions about building safety, construction oversight, inspections and the protection of residents in densely populated neighbourhoods.

WHAT HAPPENS NEXT: Investigators will need to establish the sequence of events, assess the structural condition of the building and determine whether any safety rules were breached.

articles.title: Pope Leo Receives Major Public Welcome During Peru Visit
articles.excerpt: The Pope has drawn a large crowd during his visit to Peru and spoken of his personal connection to the country.
articles.content:
Pope Leo has received a major public welcome during his visit to Peru. Reuters reported that the crowd was the largest of his papacy so far as he returned to a country with which he has a strong personal connection.

The visit places attention on the Catholic Church's relationship with communities across Latin America and the social challenges facing the region. Public engagement during papal visits can provide an opportunity to address poverty, inequality, migration and the role of religious institutions in public life.

WHY IT MATTERS: The visit is significant both for the Catholic community and for the Pope's engagement with Latin America. It also highlights the continuing influence of religious institutions in social and humanitarian discussions.

WHAT HAPPENS NEXT: The focus will be on the messages delivered during the visit and the Pope's meetings with religious and civic representatives.

articles.title: COP31 Negotiations Face Pressure to Turn Climate Pledges into Action
articles.excerpt: Governments are under pressure to demonstrate progress on climate finance, adaptation and emissions reduction at the UN climate conference in Türkiye.
articles.content:
The United Nations climate conference, COP31, is taking place in Antalya, Türkiye, against a backdrop of growing pressure on governments to turn long-term climate promises into measurable action.

Negotiations are focused on the transition away from fossil fuels, adaptation to climate impacts and the financing needed by vulnerable countries. Developing nations continue to argue that commitments must translate into accessible funding and practical support for communities already experiencing the effects of climate change.

The central challenge is implementation. Announced financial commitments must be assessed against the amount actually made available, the conditions attached to funding and the communities that receive support.

WHY IT MATTERS: Climate change affects food security, infrastructure, health, migration and economic stability. Countries with fewer resources often face some of the greatest risks.

WHAT HAPPENS NEXT: Negotiators will be judged on whether the conference produces practical commitments, credible financing arrangements and clear mechanisms for monitoring progress.

radiantWavesPerspective.title: RadiantWaves Perspective — The Test Is Delivery and Accountability
radiantWavesPerspective.content:
Today's developments show how quickly decisions made in capitals affect ordinary people. Diplomatic meetings may open doors, but they must produce verifiable steps towards peace. A prisoner exchange is important, but it is not a ceasefire. Civilian hospitals must be protected, and claims about military targets must be independently examined. Political transitions must follow constitutional procedures.

In Nigeria, the ADC dispute should be reported through the court record, the appeal process and the actions of INEC, not through partisan assumptions. In France, the presidential debate should be judged by policy and public support rather than celebrity or endorsement alone. In Africa, the Ebola response demonstrates why public-health surveillance and cross-border cooperation remain essential.

RadiantWaves Media will continue to distinguish established facts from allegations, official explanations and political arguments. Our reporting will ask what happened, who made the decision, what evidence is available, what remains uncertain and what consequences may follow.

sourcePolicy.title: Our Editorial and Source Policy
sourcePolicy.content: RadiantWaves Media reports and explains developments using named, credible news organisations, official institutions and primary statements where available. Sources are identified in our reports for transparency; our reporting is independently written and contextualised. Allegations are attributed to the people or institutions making them and are not presented as established facts. Court decisions, appeals and pending proceedings are distinguished. Figures and claims that remain disputed or independently unverified are labelled accordingly. We update coverage when material new information is confirmed.
